name: Testicular Regression Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Surgical Diagnostic Criteria for Testicular Regression Syndrome

criteria.description: Absence of one or both testes on physical examination and surgical exploration
Presence of fibrous or nodule-like remnants of testicular tissue on histopathology
Absence of persistent Müllerian duct structures confirming normal anti-Müllerian hormone function

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Absence of testis confirmed by surgical exploration plus histopathological evidence of testicular remnants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed during surgery for non-palpable testis; imaging alone is insufficient.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal morphology of female internal genitalia

laboratory: Elevated serum LH and FSH in bilateral cases
Normal or mildly elevated testosterone in unilateral cases
imaging: Ultrasound showing absent or hypoplastic testis
MRI may be used to identify testicular remnants
other: Histopathology revealing fibrous or calcified testicular remnants

distinguishingFeatures: Palpable or detectable testis on imaging or surgery
Complete absence of testicular tissue without remnants
Confirmed by surgical exploration and histology

redFlags: Bilateral non-palpable testes with micropenis indicating possible endocrine dysfunction
Absence of testicular tissue on surgical exploration without histological remnants
Delayed puberty or signs of androgen deficiency in adolescence
references: Baskin LS. Cryptorchidism and testicular regression syndrome. Urol Clin North Am. 2010
Hadziselimovic F. Testicular regression syndrome: clinical and histological aspects. J Urol. 1991
